title: THE FIRST MURDERER.
paragraphs: THE FIRST MURDERER.

Not a thief.
Not a liar.
A killer.
The first human being to spill human blood.
His name was Cain.
And what God did next… shocks people who have only heard half the story.
Because after Cain murdered his own brother Abel, God confronted him:
“Where is your brother?” (Genesis 4:9)

Cain lied.
Deflected.
Hardened his heart.
Then the judgment came.

The ground would resist him.
The land would reject him.
His life would become wandering.
But then Cain said something revealing:
“My punishment is greater than I can bear… whoever finds me will kill me.” (Genesis 4:13–14)
Now watch this carefully.
God did not excuse the murder.
But He also did not abandon Cain to revenge.
Instead Scripture says:
“The Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.” (Genesis 4:15)
Let that settle in your spirit.
The first murderer in human history…
was still protected by God.
Why?
Because from the very beginning, God was showing something about His heart:

Justice is real.
Sin has consequences.
But vengeance belongs to God—not man.
Even in the shadow of the first murder, God restrained the spiral of human violence.
And hidden inside this dark story is a whisper of the Gospel.

Abel’s blood cried out from the ground for justice.
But the blood of Jesus speaks something greater.
Hebrews 12:24 says the blood of Christ “speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.”
Abel’s blood cried for judgment.
Jesus’ blood cries for mercy.
That means this:
If God restrained vengeance even for Cain…
how much more mercy is available through Jesus Christ?
Your past may accuse you.
Your guilt may whisper: You’ve gone too far.
But the cross declares something stronger.
Grace is louder than your worst moment.
And Jesus still receives sinners who turn back to Him.
So today the invitation is simple:
Come out of hiding.

Bring the sin.
Bring the shame.
Bring the story you think God cannot redeem.
Because the same God who marked Cain with protection…
sent His Son to mark you with salvation.
And His blood still speaks.
Mercy.
Repent, and come to Christ.
